name: Teen Do Panch (3-2-5)
description: 3-2-5 (Teen Do Panch, also 2-3-5 or 5-3-2) is a trick-taking card game played in India, Pakistan, and Nepal. Three players use a 30-card deck. Each has a trick quota: dealer 2, player to dealer's right 5, player to dealer's left 3. The 5-trick player chooses trump and leads. Players above quota can 'pull' cards from those below in the next deal.
deck: 30 cards (remove 2s–6s from 52; keep 7s of hearts and spades). Rank: A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7.

history.origins: South Asia (India, Pakistan, Nepal). Closely related to Sergeant Major (3-5-8 / 8-5-3) played with 52 cards.
timeline: 2020: English-language rules for 3-2-5 were published online, clearly describing quotas, trump selection, and the card-pulling mechanism.
history.cultural: Popular in India, Pakistan, and Nepal; often played counter-clockwise.
history.evolution: Uses 30-card pack and trick quotas; 'pulling' cards from players below quota is a distinctive feature.

setup.players: Exactly 3. Dealer has quota 2 tricks; player to dealer's right 5 tricks (chooses trump, leads); player to dealer's left 3 tricks.
setup.deck: 30-card pack: remove 2s through 6s from 52, plus remove two 7s (usually keep 7♥ and 7♠). Rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7 high to low.
setup.dealing: Three batches: 5 cards, then 3, then 2 to each player (10 each). Deal and play usually counter-clockwise.

rules.objective: Win at least your quota of tricks. Dealer 2, right of dealer 5, left of dealer 3. Player with 5-trick quota chooses trump and leads. Those above quota can pull one card per excess trick from those below quota before the next deal.
rules.gameplay: Follow suit when possible; otherwise play any card. Highest trump wins the trick, else highest card of led suit. Trick winner leads next. After the deal, players above quota may take one card from players below quota (card pulling).
keyRules: Follow suit; highest trump or led suit wins
Above quota can pull cards from below quota for next deal

strategy.basic: Choose trump to help make 5 tricks; try to avoid giving away pulls.
strategy.intermediate: Count trumps and high cards; force opponents to use trumps early.
strategy.advanced: Coordinate with position; manage when to take tricks vs. duck.
tips: Choosing weak trump with poor hand

variations.name: Clockwise Deal and Play
variations.description: Deal and play proceed clockwise instead of counter-clockwise, with the player to dealer's left taking the 5-trick quota, choosing trumps, and leading to the first trick while the player to dealer's right has the 3-trick quota.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Engine overrides for rotating deal and swapping quotas between left and right of dealer are not modeled yet; implementers should apply this variation from the textual rules.

variations.name: Seventh Card Turned for Trump
variations.description: Instead of freely announcing a trump suit, the 5-trick player may specify that the seventh card dealt to them (the middle card of the second batch of three) will be turned up and its suit becomes trumps.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Trump determination by turning the seventh card is described in rules but not wired into engine overrides; implementers can enforce it in custom logic.

variations.name: Next Batch Highest Card Trump
variations.description: Some play that the 5-trick player may choose trumps to be the suit of the highest card in the next batch of three cards dealt to them, or a randomly chosen card from the remainder of their hand.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Alternate rules where trumps follow the highest card in a later batch or a random card are not yet mapped to engine overrides; use this description when implementing variants.

variations.name: Relaxed Return Suit Requirement
variations.description: Instead of needing at least two remaining cards in the suit being returned after pulling, some play that a player who steals a card need only keep one card in that suit when choosing which card to give back.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Suit-retention constraint for returned cards can be tuned in engine logic; this variation documents the looser requirement but does not change engine constants yet.

variations.name: Sevens as Permanent Trumps
variations.description: In some circles both Sevens are permanent trumps: the 7 of hearts is the highest trump, followed by the 7 of spades, then the remaining cards of the chosen trump suit in their usual order.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Permanent-trump treatment of the Sevens affects trick resolution but is not reflected in engine overrides; implementers must handle this ranking rule explicitly.

variations.name: Bonus for Winning All Ten Tricks
variations.description: Some players award an extra 5 points, for a total of 15, to any player who succeeds in winning all ten tricks in a deal.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Scoring for slam bonuses is not parameterized in engine overrides for this game; this variation documents the extra points rule for implementers.

variations.name: Trick Transfer and Loser Deals
variations.description: Variants allow a below-quota player to transfer a trick to an above-quota player instead of giving up a card and may also make the biggest loser of a deal the next dealer instead of rotating the deal normally.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variants that transfer tricks instead of cards and use the losing player as next dealer are described but not encoded in engine overrides; apply them directly in game logic if needed.

scoring.description: No point scoring—meeting or exceeding trick quota matters; pulling cards is the penalty/reward.
scoring.winCondition: Win at least your quota of tricks. Dealer 2, right of dealer 5, left of dealer 3. Player with 5-trick quota chooses trump and leads. Those above quota can pull one card per excess trick from those below quota before the next deal.
